sents.d: A consistent routine reduces impulsive, reactive decisions.

Many experienced traders describe using some form of pre-market routine — reviewing relevant news, checking key levels on their watchlist, and confirming their plan for the day before markets open, rather than reacting in real time with no preparation.

This routine doesn't need to be lengthy; even 10-15 minutes of preparation can reduce the likelihood of impulsive decisions once the trading day is underway and emotions are more likely to be involved.
Reviewing the previous day's trades as part of this routine — what worked, what didn't — turns the routine into an ongoing learning loop rather than just a checklist.

take: A short pre-market routine reduces impulsive decisions.
